Vorlage Typ-Nr. Spaltenformat MwSt. je Satz QR-Code Download Rechnung 0 1,2,4,5,7,6 ja ja Demo-00-Rechnung.odt Rechnung Kleinunternehmer (§ 19 UStG, ohne USt.) 0 1,2,4,5,6 – ja Demo-00-Rechnung-Kleinunternehmer.odt Auftrag 1 1,2,4,5,7,6 ja – Demo-01-Auftrag.odt Angebot 2 1,2,4,5,7,6 ja – Demo-02-Angebot.odt Lieferschein 3 1,2,4,5,7,6 ja – Demo-03-Lieferschein.odt Auftragsbestätigung 4 1,2,4,5,7,6 ja – Demo-04-Auftragsbestaetigung.odt Artikeldatenblatt 5 – – – Demo-05-Artikeldatenblatt.odt Leistungsbeschreibung 6 – – – Demo-06-Leistungsbeschreibung.odt Mahnung 7 – – – Demo-07-Mahnung-zu-Rechnung.odt Kontaktdatenblatt 8 – – – Demo-08-Kontaktdatenblatt.odt Journal 9 6,9,10,1,8,11,12,13,14,15 – – Demo-09-Journal.odt Bestellung 10 1,2,4,5,6 – – Demo-10-Bestellung.odt Vertrag 11 1,2,4,5,7,6 ja – Demo-11-Vertrag.odt Gesprächsnotiz 12 – – – Demo-12-Gespraechsnotiz.odt Serienbrief 13 – – – Demo-13-Serienbrief.odt Tätigkeitsliste 14 1,2,4,5,9 – – Demo-14-Taetigkeitsliste.odt Gutschrift 20 1,2,4,5,7,6 ja – Demo-20-Gutschrift.odt Abschlagsrechnung 21 1,2,4,5,7,6 ja ja Demo-21-Abschlagsrechnung.odt Anzahlungsrechnung 22 1,2,4,5,7,6 ja ja Demo-22-Anzahlungsrechnung.odt Kassenbon (Kasse) 0 2,4,7,9 – TSE Kassenbon.odt

Einbinden: Vorlagen-Manager › Importieren, die Datei wählen, als Art den Typ und als Format das Spaltenformat aus der Tabelle eintragen, dann dem Benutzer (und der Gruppe) zuweisen. „MwSt. je Satz“: Tabelle mit einer Zeile je Steuersatz unter den Summen (siehe unten). QR-Code: EPC-QR-Code bei Rechnungen; beim Kassenbon der QR-Code der TSE (siehe Kasse und TSE). Alle Demo-Vorlagen außer dem Journal enthalten zudem rechts neben der Überschrift den Code-39-Barcode (Barcode.img) der jeweiligen Dokument- bzw. Datensatznummer (cnumber).

docs.title: Leistungsdatum und letzte Änderung
docs.text:
Jede Rechnung muss das Datum der Lieferung oder Leistung nennen (§ 14 Abs. 4 Nr. 6 UStG). Ein Beleg hat dafür drei getrennte Daten:

Feld im Beleg Bedeutung Vorlagenfeld Belegdatum Datum der Rechnung (des Angebots …) item.dateadded Leistungsdatum Datum der Lieferung oder Leistung, änderbar. Leer: das Belegdatum (wird beim Speichern eingetragen). Bleibt beim Öffnen unverändert. In der E-Rechnung BT-72. item.servicedate (bzw. item.datetodo) Zuletzt geändert wann der Beleg zuletzt gespeichert wurde; wird automatisch gesetzt, nicht änderbar item.datelastupdated

Die Demo-Vorlagen für Rechnung, Gutschrift, Abschlags- und Anzahlungsrechnung (auch die Kleinunternehmer-Rechnung) zeigen „Leistungsdatum“ unter „Datum“.

Gutschrift / Rechnungskorrektur: <item.correctedinvoice> ist der Bezug auf die korrigierte Rechnung („Rechnung Nr. R-0042 vom 04.11.2026“, leer ohne Bezug), einzeln <item.correctedinvoicenumber> und <item.correctedinvoicedate>. Die Demo-Gutschrift trägt die Überschrift „Rechnungskorrektur“ (eine „Gutschrift“ im Sinne des UStG ist die Abrechnung durch den Leistungsempfänger, § 14 Abs. 2 Satz 2 UStG) und zeigt „Zu Rechnung“ unter dem Leistungsdatum. Unveränderte Demo-Vorlagen älterer Versionen werden beim Anmelden ersetzt; geänderte Vorlagen bleiben, dort <item.servicedate> selbst einfügen.

docs.title: Peppol-ID und EORI-Nummer
docs.text:
Für E-Rechnungen (EN 16931 BT-34 / BT-49) und die Zollabwicklung mit Drittländern stehen die Peppol-ID und die EORI-Nummer der eigenen Firma sowie des Kontakts auch als feste Vorlagenfelder zur Verfügung:

Feld Bedeutung Wo einzutragen <companyinfo.peppolid> Peppol-ID des Verkäufers (BT-34, Format <EAS>:<Kennung>) Firmeninformation › E-Rechnung (companyinfo.peppolid) <companyinfo.eori> EORI-Nummer des Verkäufers (Format a2 + an..15, z. B. DE123456789012345) Firmeninformation › Steuern (companyinfo.eori) <item.contact.peppolid> / <contact.peppolid> Peppol-ID des Käufers (BT-49, in Belegen bzw. im Kontaktdatenblatt) Kontakt › Reiter E-Rechnung / Karte Zahlung (Eigenschaft peppol-id, optional am Beleg überschreibbar) <item.contact.eori> / <contact.eori> EORI-Nummer des Kunden (in Belegen bzw. im Kontaktdatenblatt) Kontakt › Feld EORI-Nummer neben der USt-IdNr. (Eigenschaft eori)

Die Standard- und Demo-Rechnungsvorlagen zeigen die EORI-Nummer der Firma (Tabelle2) sowie die Kunden-USt-IdNr. und EORI-Nummer (<item.contact.taxnumber> <item.contact.eori>, Tabelle4, Art. 226 Abs. 4 MwStSystRL / § 14a UStG) automatisch an. In E-Rechnungen (XRechnung / ZUGFeRD) werden die Peppol-IDs als elektronische Adressen (URIUniversalCommunication mit schemeID) und vorhandene EORI-Nummern als EN-16931-Zollvermerk (BG-1 / BT-21 = CUS) ausgegeben; siehe E-Rechnung.

docs.title: Außenhandel, Zoll & Handelsrechnung
docs.text:
Für den Export in Drittländer und die Zollabwicklung stehen zusätzliche Beleg- und Artikelfelder sowie eine zweisprachige Handelsrechnung (Demo-00-Handelsrechnung-Export.odt / demo-00-commercial.odt) zur Verfügung:

Feld Bedeutung Wo einzutragen <item.currency> ISO-4217-Währungscode (BT-5, z. B. EUR, CHF, USD) Beleg-Eigenschaft currency, sonst Währungs-Auswahl am Kontakt (bankcurrency) oder Kontakt-Eigenschaft currency, Fallback EUR <item.incoterms> Incoterms® + benannter Ort (z. B. DAP Zürich) Eigenschaft incoterms am Beleg oder Kontakt <item.netweight> Gesamt-Eigenmasse (kg); ohne Überschreibung automatisch aus den verknüpften Produktgewichten summiert Beleg-Eigenschaft netweight (optional) <item.grossweight> Gesamt-Rohmasse (kg) Beleg-Eigenschaft grossweight <item.packages> Anzahl / Art der Packstücke Beleg-Eigenschaft packages <product.hscode> Zolltarifnummer / HS-Code (BT-158, 4–11 Ziffern) Produkt (moderne Ansicht › Einordnung) <product.origincountry> Ursprungsland (BT-159, ISO-3166-Alpha-2) Produkt (moderne Ansicht › Einordnung) <product.netweight> Eigenmasse pro Einheit (kg) Produkt (moderne Ansicht › Einordnung)

In der Positionstabelle (xtable1) stehen zusätzlich die Spalten 14 (Zolltarifnr. (HS-Code)), 15 (Ursprungsland) und 16 (Eigenmasse (kg) der Position = Stückgewicht × Menge) im Vorlagen-Manager zur Auswahl.

docs.title: MwSt. je Steuersatz (§ 14 Abs. 4 Nr. 8 UStG)
docs.text:
Enthält eine Rechnung Positionen mit verschiedenen Steuersätzen (z. B. 19 % und 7 %), müssen Nettobetrag und Steuerbetrag je Steuersatz ausgewiesen werden. Die Steuer wird je Satz auf die Summe der Nettobeträge gerechnet und einmal gerundet – genau wie in der E-Rechnung (ZUGFeRD / XRechnung, ApplicableTradeTax), so stimmen PDF und XML auf den Cent überein.

Tabelle mit einer Zeile je Steuersatz: eine Tabellenzeile mit Platzhaltern vatgroups.* wird für jeden Steuersatz wiederholt (höchster Satz zuerst):

Steuersatz Netto MwSt. Brutto <vatgroups.name> <vatgroups.netf> <vatgroups.vatf> <vatgroups.grossf> Gesamt <item.netvaluef> <item.taxvaluef> <item.grosvaluef> Feld Inhalt vatgroups.rate Steuersatz, z. B. 19,00 % vatgroups.ratevalue Steuersatz als Zahl, z. B. 19 oder 7.7 vatgroups.name Name des Steuersatzes aus Einstellungen › Steuersätze, sonst MwSt. 19,00 % bzw. Steuerfrei vatgroups.net / vatgroups.netf Summe netto des Satzes (Zahl / mit Währung) vatgroups.vat / vatgroups.vatf Steuerbetrag des Satzes vatgroups.gross / vatgroups.grossf Summe brutto des Satzes

Feste Felder (z. B. für Vorlagen mit festem Layout): item.vatgroup1.rate, item.vatgroup1.netf, item.vatgroup1.vatf, item.vatgroup1.grossf … und ebenso item.vatgroup2.*, item.vatgroup3.* (dieselben Namen wie oben). Dazu item.vatgroupcount (Anzahl der Steuersätze) und item.hasmultipletaxrates (true / false).

Ältere Vorlagen funktionieren unverändert: item.tax (Steuersatz, bei mehreren Sätzen der niedrigste), item.taxgroup1, item.taxgroupvalue1 … und item.taxgroups (Text mit allen Sätzen) bleiben, wie sie waren. Bereits importierte Vorlagen und ihr Spaltenformat werden nicht geändert; die neuen Demo-Vorlagen lassen sich im Vorlagen-Manager importieren.

docs.title: Eigene Vorlagenfelder (Eigenschaften)
docs.text: Neben den festen Feldern lassen sich eigene Felder mit frei gewähltem Namen anlegen. In der Vorlage heißen sie immer <…property.NAME>.

docs.title: Wo man sie anlegt
docs.text:
Wo Gilt für Feld in der Vorlage Kontakt › Bereich Eigenschaften (Name, Wert) diesen einen Kontakt Belege: <item.contact.property.NAME>, Kontaktdatenblatt: <contact.property.NAME> Systemsteuerung › Skriptmanager, „Für“ und Gruppe wählen (siehe Skripte) – bevorzugt alle Datensätze dieser Art und Gruppe, z. B. Alle Belege Kontakt: wie oben; Beleg: <item.property.NAME>; Artikel / Leistung: <product.property.NAME>
  • Im Kontakt werden die Eigenschaften mit dem Kontakt gespeichert. Ein mit eingegebenes Präfix (contact.property.anrede, <item.contact.property.anrede>) wird entfernt – gespeichert wird anrede. Testen… zeigt alle Felder des Kontakts, wie sie in einer Rechnung heißen (<item.contact.…>), mit ihren Werten (Skripte ausgeführt).
  • NAME nur aus Buchstaben und Ziffern, am besten klein geschrieben. Namen, die mit modify oder execute beginnen, sind Skripte, die beim Speichern laufen – sie werden kein Vorlagenfeld.
  • Das Präfix vor .property. ist das Präfix des Datensatzes in der Vorlage: Der Kontakt eines Belegs ist item.contact, also <item.contact.property.anrede> – nicht item.contact.anrede und nicht contact.property.anrede (das gilt nur im Kontaktdatenblatt).
  • Artikel haben keinen eigenen Bereich Eigenschaften; Artikelfelder legt man im Skriptmanager an. Sie stehen im Artikeldatenblatt / in der Leistungsbeschreibung zur Verfügung, nicht in den Positionen eines Belegs.

docs.title: Fester Text oder Skript
docs.text:
• Ein normaler Wert (z. B. 2 Wochen) erscheint unverändert.
  • Ein Wert, der mit # beginnt und endet, ist ein Groovy-Skript; in die Vorlage kommt sein Ergebnis. Im Skriptmanager wird das # automatisch ergänzt – dort nur das Skript selbst eintragen. Im Bereich Eigenschaften muss man die # selbst schreiben. Innerhalb des Skripts darf kein # vorkommen.
  • Im Skript heißen die Felder wie in der Vorlage, ohne <>:
  • in einem Kontaktfeld: contact.cname, contact.prename, contact.ismale, contact.property.lieferzeit …
  • in einem Belegfeld: item.cnumber, item.netvalue, item.contact.cname, item.contact.ismale, item.contact.property.anrede …
  • in einem Artikelfeld: product.cnumber, product.externalnetvalue …

Es sind die Rohwerte: ismale ist true/false (in der Vorlage 1/0), Beträge sind Zahlen. Formatierte Felder (item.netvaluef) gibt es mit getFormField('item.netvaluef'). Verfügbar sind die Felder des Datensatzes, dem das Feld gehört, und alles, was daran hängt – in einem Kontaktfeld gibt es also contact.…, aber kein item.…, auch wenn der Kontakt gerade in einer Rechnung gedruckt wird. - Außerdem: dbo – der Datensatz selbst (z. B. dbo.__getCname()), getObject('contact', 'Name') – ein anderer Datensatz. - Schlägt ein Skript fehl (z. B. eine unbekannte Variable), erscheint der Skripttext unverändert im Dokument – das ist der Hinweis, das Skript zu prüfen (Mit einem Datensatz testen… im Skriptmanager).

docs.title: Beispiele
docs.text:
Briefanrede je Kontakt – im Kontakt unter Eigenschaften:

Name Wert anrede #contact.ismale ? "Sehr geehrter Herr " + contact.cname + "," : "Sehr geehrte Frau " + contact.cname + ","#

In der Rechnungsvorlage: <item.contact.property.anrede> → Sehr geehrter Herr Müller,

Dasselbe für alle Kontakte – im Skriptmanager: Art Kontakt, Gruppe Alle Gruppen, Name anrede, Skript (ohne #):

contact.ismale ? "Sehr geehrter Herr " + contact.cname + "," : "Sehr geehrte Frau " + contact.cname + ","

Fester Wert je Kontakt – Name lieferzeit, Wert 2 Wochen; in der Vorlage <item.contact.property.lieferzeit>.

Feld am Beleg mit Daten des Kontakts – Skriptmanager, Art Rechnung, Name gruss:

(item.contact.ismale ? "Lieber Herr " : "Liebe Frau ") + item.contact.cname

In der Vorlage: <item.property.gruss>.

Artikelfeld – Skriptmanager, Art Artikel, Name hinweis: "Artikel " + product.cnumber + " – Preis zzgl. Versand"; im Artikeldatenblatt <product.property.hinweis>.

docs.title: Bilder in Vorlagen
docs.text:
Bildname Inhalt Barcode.img (oder Code39.img) Code-39-Barcode der Dokument- bzw. Datensatznummer (cnumber, z. B. item.cnumber, contact.cnumber, product.cnumber, reminder.item.cnumber) mit Klartextzeile darunter QRCode.img EPC-QR-Code (GiroCode) auf Rechnungen – siehe QR-Code TSEQRCode.img QR-Code der TSE-Daten auf dem Kassenbon – siehe Kasse und TSE

Den Namen vergibt man in LibreOffice unter Bild › Eigenschaften › Optionen › Name (die im Dokument eingestellte Rahmengröße bleibt erhalten, z. B. 5,0 × 1,0 cm für den Barcode). Ohne Daten – oder wenn die Nummer nicht in Code 39 darstellbar ist – wird das Bild entfernt.

Code-39-Hinweise: Unterstützt werden 0–9, A–Z, -, ., Leerzeichen, $, /, +, % bis 80 Zeichen; Kleinbuchstaben werden automatisch in Großbuchstaben umgewandelt, Start-/Stoppzeichen (*) ergänzt YaBS automatisch. Alle Demo-Vorlagen (außer dem Journal) enthalten Barcode.img bereits rechts neben der Überschrift.

docs.title: Demo-Vorlagen neu erzeugen
docs.text:
Die Vorlagen werden aus der deutschen Standardvorlage src/main/resources/extra/DE-Yabs-2.0.odt erzeugt; die Feldlisten kommen aus der Datenbankstruktur:

python3 tools/templates/gen.py .

Ergebnis: src/main/resources/extra/templates/demo-XX.odt (XX = Typ-Nr.) und die Kopien zum Herunterladen in tools/templates/ (siehe oben). Logo: tools/templates/logo.png, Barcode-Platzhalter: tools/templates/barcode.png. Danach neu bauen; bestehende Installationen importieren die Vorlagen nicht automatisch (Vorlagen-Manager › Importieren).

docs.title: Writing plugins
docs.text: Deutsch: Plugins schreiben

docs.title: Writing Plugins for OpenYaBS
docs.text:
OpenYaBS plugins extend the application without touching the core codebase. Using a single, unified API — ExtensionContext — a plugin can add:

  • Commands (in the Plugins menu and in Search anything via Shift Shift)
  • Custom search results in Search anything
  • Settings pages (under Settings › Plugins, searchable via the settings search bar)
  • Custom tabs in the main window
  • View decorations & locks (header badges, banners with action buttons, content locks on record views)
  • Activity reactions (new/changed/deleted records, exported PDF/ODT/e-invoice files, messages)
  • Record interceptors (validate, modify, or veto saving and deleting of records)
  • Custom template placeholders ([myplugin.key] in LibreOffice .odt/.fodt templates)
  • Journal exports & tax-adviser ZIP entries (extra items in the Journal Export menu and files inside the tax-adviser ZIP)
  • Pre-send e-mail warnings (interactive confirmation or batch skip for sensitive documents)
  • E-invoice skip rules (fall back to plain PDF instead of ZUGFeRD / XRechnung for matching invoices)
  • GDPR / privacy integration (custom retention deadlines, Art. 15/20 export files, cleanup on final deletion)
  • Archived originals for locked documents (serve immutable originals and control stamped duplicates)
  • Plugin-scoped internationalization (i18n) (automatic locale resolution, MessageFormat arguments, zero key collisions)

Plugins can be written either as a single Groovy script (.groovy, zero build step) or as a Java JAR (.jar, full IDE & build tooling). Both receive the exact same ExtensionContext API.

docs.title: How Plugins Work in OpenYaBS
docs.text:
• Location: Plugins live in the plugins/ directory inside your YaBS application folder (Settings › Plugins › Open folder).
  • Management UI: Settings › Plugins lists every built-in, Groovy, and Java plugin with its state (RUNNING, STOPPED, DISABLED, FAILED), addition count, and error message if failed. Under Add a plugin, you can click New Groovy plugin…, Import Groovy plugin…, Import Java plugin…, or simply drag and drop a .groovy or .jar file onto the page.
  • Non-blocking startup: After login, OpenYaBS discovers plugins and compiles Groovy scripts in a background thread (yabs-plugins), showing progress in the status bar (Loading plugins (2/5): …), then calls each plugin's start(ctx) sequentially on the Swing Event Dispatch Thread (EDT).
  • Fault isolation: If a plugin throws an exception in start(ctx) or fails its minYabsVersion() check, any partial registrations are rolled back, the plugin is marked FAILED with its error message, and OpenYaBS and all other plugins continue normally.
  • Automatic cleanup & hot reload: Every contribution registered through ExtensionContext is owned by the plugin's id and automatically removed when the plugin stops, is disabled, reloaded, uninstalled, or fails to start. You can iterate and reload plugins without restarting OpenYaBS.
  • Database switching: When the user switches to or creates another database connection, OpenYaBS calls stopAll() and then startAllInBackground(). Always guard database access in start(ctx) so your plugin handles reconnects and headless test runs cleanly.
  • Plugin IDs & seamless replacement: Every plugin must have a unique, stable id(). Two plugins with the same ID never run simultaneously. Installing a new file whose plugin has the same ID as an existing file (for example, upgrading a Groovy prototype to a Java JAR) automatically stops the old plugin, activates the new one, and renames the old file to <filename>.replaced.
  • Per-plugin files on disk: Inside plugins/, OpenYaBS manages:
  • plugins.properties — comma-separated list of disabled plugin IDs
  • <safe-plugin-id>.properties — key/value store returned by ctx.settings()
  • <safe-plugin-id>/ — private directory returned by ctx.dataFolder() (created on demand)

docs.title: Groovy vs. Java: Pros, Cons, and Decision Guide
docs.text: Both Groovy and Java plugins have full access to ExtensionContext and all OpenYaBS classes. The difference is developer workflow, packaging, performance, and maintainability.

docs.title: Side-by-Side Comparison
docs.text: Aspect Groovy Plugin (.groovy) Java Plugin (.jar) API entry point Script variable yabs (ExtensionContext) and plugin (GroovyExtension) YabsExtension.start(ExtensionContext ctx) Metadata Header comments: // @id, @name, @description, @version, @author, @minYabsVersion Interface methods: id(), name(), description(), version(), author(), minYabsVersion() Stop hook onStop = { … } or yabs.onStop { … } stop() and/or ctx.onStop(() -> …) Build toolchain None — edit and save a plain text file JDK 21 + Gradle (or Maven / javac + jar) Reload cycle Instant (Ctrl+S in the built-in editor) Rebuild JAR → copy / import → click Reload Built-in editor Yes (Settings › Plugins › Edit): syntax highlighting, line numbers, F5 syntax check, snippets No — use IntelliJ IDEA, VS Code, Eclipse, or CLI + AI agent Type safety Dynamic typing (runtime errors for typos unless @CompileStatic is used) Full compile-time type checking and IDE refactoring Startup overhead Parsed and compiled by GroovyShell on every app start (noticeable for large scripts) Pre-compiled bytecode — near-instant load Code organization Single .groovy file (editor disables highlighting above ~60,000 chars) Unlimited packages, classes, helpers, and clean separation of concerns Bundled resources Not supported natively (must embed as strings or ship separate files) Native JAR resources (getResourceAsStream): .fodt templates, i18n/*.properties, JSON catalogs, icons Third-party libraries No @Grab (Apache Ivy is intentionally excluded from OpenYaBS); limited to JDK + bundled OpenYaBS libs Full support — bundle extra dependencies in a fat/shaded JAR if needed Multiple plugins per file 1 plugin per .groovy file Multiple YabsExtension implementations in one JAR (one class per line in META-INF/services/…) Unit testing & CI Possible via ExtensionManager.install(file), harder to unit-test internal helpers First-class JUnit 5 testing of pure logic, SQL against H2, and headless ExtensionManager Distribution Share one .groovy file; users can inspect/tweak directly Share one .jar file; clean versioning and reproducible builds

docs.title: Groovy Plugins — Pros & Cons
docs.text:
Pros: - Zero setup: No JDK install, no Gradle, no IDE required — anyone running OpenYaBS can write and run a plugin in 30 seconds. - Built-in editor: Includes Groovy syntax highlighting, line numbers, working code snippets (Insert example), F5 compile check with jump-to-line error reporting, and Ctrl+S instant reload. - Concise syntax: Groovy closures automatically coerce to Java functional interfaces (Runnable, Consumer, Function, Predicate, Supplier), and dynamic property access makes quick experiments effortless. - Great for AI quick-fixes & automations: An AI agent can generate a single self-contained .groovy file that the user drops straight into plugins/ without running a build tool.

Cons: - Runtime-only error detection: Misspelled method names or wrong argument types only fail when that code path executes. - No bundled resources: Shipping LibreOffice .fodt templates, .properties translation files, or JSON catalogs is awkward compared to a JAR. - No @Grab / external dependencies: Apache Ivy is excluded from OpenYaBS's Groovy runtime, so Groovy plugins can only use the JDK and libraries already bundled in OpenYaBS's lib/. - Does not scale well to large plugins: Startup compilation takes seconds for large scripts, single-file navigation becomes painful, and the built-in editor turns off syntax highlighting above ~60,000 characters.

docs.title: Java Plugins — Pros & Cons
docs.text:
Pros: - Compile-time safety: The Java 21 compiler catches API mismatches, missing imports, and wrong types before the plugin ever runs. - Clean multi-class architecture: Separate persistence (Store), pure business logic (Validator), Swing UI (Ui), and entry point (Plugin), just like all official OpenYaBS plugins. - First-class resources & i18n: Bundle .fodt/.odt templates, UTF-8 messages_en.properties / messages_de.properties files, JSON data catalogs, and icons directly inside src/main/resources/. - Fast startup & high performance: Pre-compiled bytecode loads cleanly through an isolated URLClassLoader. - Full automated testing: Write fast JUnit 5 tests for validators, SQL queries (against in-memory H2), i18n bundles, and headless ExtensionManager lifecycle checks — ideal for AI coding agents running ./gradlew test in a loop! - Third-party libraries: If you need a library not shipped with OpenYaBS, you can shade/bundle it inside your plugin JAR.

Cons: - Requires a build toolchain: Needs JDK 21 and Gradle (or Maven) to compile and package the JAR. - Slightly slower manual edit-test loop: Requires running ./gradlew jar and clicking Reload (though automated JUnit tests largely offset this).

docs.title: Decision Guide: When to Choose Which?
docs.text: Choose Groovy if… Choose Java if… You want a small automation (< ~300 lines): custom command, notification, quick search provider, simple save rule. You are building a domain/industry module (custom DB tables, dialogs, reports, exports, templates). You want to prototype an idea live inside OpenYaBS without setting up a build environment. You want to ship .fodt templates, multi-language .properties bundles, or data catalogs inside one JAR. The end user should be able to open and tweak the script directly in Settings › Plugins › Edit. You want compile-time verification, JUnit 5 tests, Git/CI workflows, or reliable distribution to many users. You are only using OpenYaBS's built-in classes and JDK APIs. You need third-party libraries or multiple classes/packages.

docs.title: Seamless Migration Path: Groovy → Java
docs.text:
You can safely start in Groovy and later rewrite the plugin in Java without breaking existing installations:

  1. In your Java YabsExtension, return the exact same id() that the Groovy script used (e.g. "groovy.my-plugin" or your custom // @id).
  2. When the user installs the new .jar via Settings › Plugins › Import Java plugin…, OpenYaBS automatically stops the Groovy plugin, activates the Java plugin, and renames my-plugin.groovy to my-plugin.groovy.replaced.
  3. Because ctx.settings(), ctx.dataFolder(), and any custom database tables are keyed by id(), all user settings, files, and data are preserved seamlessly. (The official GoBD plugin uses this exact mechanism with ID = "groovy.gobd-compliance".)

docs.title: Option A: Using the Built-In Plugin Editor
docs.text:
1. Open Settings › Plugins and click New Groovy plugin….
  2. Enter a name (e.g. invoice-helper). OpenYaBS creates plugins/invoice-helper.groovy from a working template and opens the Groovy Plugin Editor.
  3. Use Insert example ▾ to insert working snippets (command, search provider, activity listener, settings page, custom tab, record modifier, stored settings, background task).
  4. Press F5 (Check) to syntax-check in the background (errors jump straight to the offending line).
  5. Press Ctrl+S (Save and start) to save and immediately hot-reload the plugin. Click Other editor to edit the file in VS Code / IntelliJ / your system editor instead.

docs.title: Option B: Creating a File Directly in plugins/
docs.text:
Create plugins/invoice-helper.groovy (UTF-8):

// @id com.example.invoice-helper
// @name Invoice Helper
// @description Notifies on new invoices and adds a quick lookup command
// @version 1.0.0
// @author Your Name
// @minYabsVersion 2.0.10

import mpv5.db.common.Context
import mpv5.db.common.DatabaseObject
import mpv5.db.objects.Item
import mpv5.handler.Activity
import mpv5.plugin.api.SearchResult

// 1. Register a command in the "Plugins" menu and "Search anything" (Shift Shift)
yabs.addCommand('Count open invoices', 'Counts all unpaid invoices in the background', {
    yabs.background({
        def all = DatabaseObject.getObjects(Context.getInvoice())
        all.count { Item inv ->
            inv.__getIntstatus() != Item.STATUS_PAID && inv.__getIntstatus() != Item.STATUS_CANCELLED
        }
    }, { openCount ->
        yabs.notify("Open invoices: ${openCount}")
    })
})

// 2. React to newly created invoices (locale-independent via Context!)
yabs.onActivity({ Activity.Entry entry ->
    if (entry.kind == Activity.Kind.CREATED && Context.getInvoice().equals(entry.context)) {
        yabs.notify("New invoice created: ${entry.text}")
    }
})

// 3. Add custom results to "Search anything" (runs on a background thread)
yabs.addSearchProvider({ String query ->
    if (query == null || !query.toLowerCase().startsWith('open ')) {
        return []
    }
    def needle = query.substring(5).trim().toLowerCase()
    if (needle.isEmpty()) {
        return []
    }
    [new SearchResult("Search web for '${needle}'", 'Opens in default browser', {
        java.awt.Desktop.desktop.browse(new URI('https://duckduckgo.com/?q=' + URLEncoder.encode(needle, 'UTF-8')))
    } as Runnable)]
})

// 4. Optional cleanup when the plugin stops (disabled, reloaded, or app closes)
onStop = {
    // Only needed for resources you created yourself (timers, threads, sockets).
    // Commands, listeners, and providers registered via 'yabs' are removed automatically.
}

Save the file, then click Reload in Settings › Plugins (or restart OpenYaBS).

docs.title: Groovy Plugin Details & Rules
docs.text:
• Header tags: Must appear at the very top of the file as // @key value. Parsing stops at the first line that is neither blank nor a // comment. Keys are case-insensitive:
  • @id — stable unique ID (defaults to groovy.<filename-without-extension>)
  • @name — display name (defaults to <filename-without-extension>)
  • @description — short description (defaults to "")
  • @version — version string (defaults to "1.0")
  • @author — author name (defaults to "")
  • @minYabsVersion (aliases: @minYabs, @minVersion) — minimum OpenYaBS release version (defaults to null, i.e., any version)
  • Bound variables:
  • yabs — the ExtensionContext
  • plugin — the GroovyExtension wrapper itself
  • Returning a YabsExtension object: Instead of calling yabs.* at top level, a Groovy script may return an object implementing mpv5.plugin.api.YabsExtension. OpenYaBS will then delegate name(), description(), version(), author(), minYabsVersion(), start(ctx), and stop() to that object (note that id() is still read from @id or groovy.<filename> before execution).

docs.title: 2. Implement YabsExtension
docs.text:
src/main/java/com/example/myplugin/HelloPlugin.java:

package com.example.myplugin;

import mpv5.plugin.api.ExtensionContext;
import mpv5.plugin.api.YabsExtension;

public final class HelloPlugin implements YabsExtension {

    public static final String ID = "com.example.hello";
    private ExtensionContext ctx;

    @Override
    public String id() {
        return ID;
    }

    @Override
    public String name() {
        return ctx != null ? ctx.tr("plugin.name") : "Hello Plugin";
    }

    @Override
    public String description() {
        return ctx != null ? ctx.tr("plugin.description") : "Example Java plugin for OpenYaBS.";
    }

    @Override
    public String version() {
        return "1.0.0";
    }

    @Override
    public String author() {
        return "Your Name";
    }

    @Override
    public String minYabsVersion() {
        return "2.0.10";
    }

    @Override
    public void start(ExtensionContext yabs) throws Exception {
        this.ctx = yabs;

        ClassLoader cl = HelloPlugin.class.getClassLoader();
        yabs.addTranslationBundle("en", "/com/example/myplugin/i18n/messages_en.properties", cl);
        yabs.addTranslationBundle("de", "/com/example/myplugin/i18n/messages_de.properties", cl);

        yabs.addCommand(
                yabs.tr("cmd.greet.title"),
                yabs.tr("cmd.greet.desc"),
                () -> yabs.notify(yabs.tr("cmd.greet.msg", yabs.yabsVersion())));

        yabs.onStop(() -> {
            // Release any custom threads, timers, or connections here.
        });
    }

    @Override
    public void stop() {
        this.ctx = null;
    }
}

docs.title: 3. Register via Java ServiceLoader
docs.text:
Create src/main/resources/META-INF/services/mpv5.plugin.api.YabsExtension with one fully qualified class name per line:

com.example.myplugin.HelloPlugin

Note: A single JAR may list multiple YabsExtension classes (one per line). They share one URLClassLoader and are reloaded or uninstalled together. If META-INF/services/mpv5.plugin.api.YabsExtension is missing or empty, OpenYaBS rejects the JAR on import.

docs.title: 4. build.gradle (Standalone)
docs.text:
Point openyabsDir at an extracted OpenYaBS installation (containing openyabs.jar and lib/*.jar) or a local OpenYaBS build (build/libs):

plugins {
    id 'java'
}

group = 'com.example'
version = '1.0.0'

def openyabsDir = findProperty('openyabsDir') ?: '/path/to/openyabs'

java {
    toolchain {
        languageVersion = JavaLanguageVersion.of(21)
    }
}

tasks.withType(JavaCompile).configureEach {
    options.release = 21
    options.encoding = 'UTF-8'
}

repositories {
    mavenCentral()
}

dependencies {
    compileOnly files("${openyabsDir}/openyabs.jar")
    compileOnly fileTree(dir: "${openyabsDir}/lib", include: ['*.jar'])

    testImplementation platform('org.junit:junit-bom:5.10.0')
    testImplementation 'org.junit.jupiter:junit-jupiter'
    testRuntimeOnly 'org.junit.platform:junit-platform-launcher'
    testImplementation files("${openyabsDir}/openyabs.jar")
    testImplementation fileTree(dir: "${openyabsDir}/lib", include: ['*.jar'])
}

test {
    useJUnitPlatform()
}

jar {
    archiveBaseName = 'hello-plugin'
    manifest {
        attributes(
            'Implementation-Title': 'OpenYaBS Hello Plugin',
            'Implementation-Version': project.version
        )
    }
}

Build and install:

./gradlew jar

Then install build/libs/hello-plugin-1.0.0.jar via Settings › Plugins › Import Java plugin… (or drag and drop it onto the Plugins page).

Adding an official/in-repo plugin inside the openyabs repository: OpenYaBS's root build.gradle automatically discovers every subdirectory plugins/<name>/ that contains src/main/java! It creates a Gradle source set, compiles against OpenYaBS, wires it into src/test, and registers a <name>PluginJar task outputting build/plugins/<name>.jar (run ./gradlew pluginJars).

Bundling third-party dependencies: If your Java plugin depends on an external library that is not already in OpenYaBS's lib/, package it into your JAR (e.g. with the Gradle Shadow plugin or by unpacking configurations.runtimeClasspath into jar), keeping openyabs.jar and lib/*.jar as compileOnly so they are never duplicated in your plugin JAR.

docs.title: Complete API Reference
docs.text: All public plugin API classes live in package mpv5.plugin.api (browse on GitHub).

docs.title: YabsExtension and Version Compatibility
docs.text:
Source: mpv5.plugin.api.YabsExtension

Method Required? Default Description String id() Yes — Stable unique identifier (e.g. "com.example.myplugin"). Used for deduplication, replacement, settings(), dataFolder(), and i18n scoping. String name() Yes — Display name shown in Plugin Manager and Plugins menu. String description() No "" Short 1–2 sentence summary shown in Plugin Manager. String version() No "1.0" Plugin version string (e.g. "1.2.0"). String author() No "" Author or organization name. String minYabsVersion() No null Minimum required OpenYaBS version (e.g. "2.0.10"). null or empty means any version. void start(ExtensionContext ctx) throws Exception Yes — Called on the Swing EDT to initialize the plugin and register contributions. Any thrown exception marks the plugin FAILED and rolls back partial registrations. void stop() No no-op Called on the Swing EDT when the plugin stops. Contributions registered through ctx are already removed by OpenYaBS; only free resources the plugin created itself (threads, timers, sockets, keys).

How minYabsVersion() is checked: - On formal releases (e.g. 2.0.17), semantic version comparison is strictly enforced (current >= minYabsVersion). - On development/CI builds (e.g. 2.0-dev or 2.0.17-dev.123), plugins targeting the active major.minor release line are permitted so developers and CI can test upcoming features. - Pass -Dyabs.plugins.ignoreVersion=true on the JVM command line to bypass version checks during debugging.

docs.title: ExtensionContext Contributions (Auto-Removed on Stop)
docs.text:
Source: mpv5.plugin.api.ExtensionContext

Everything registered via these methods is tracked under the plugin's id() and automatically unregistered when the plugin stops, reloads, is disabled, or fails during start().

Method Callback Thread What It Does addCommand(String title, String description, Runnable action) Swing EDT Adds an action to the Plugins menu (grouped by plugin name) and to Search anything (Shift Shift). Exceptions are caught and reported without crashing OpenYaBS. addSettingsPage(String title, String description, Supplier<JComponent> page) Swing EDT Adds a page to Settings under group Plugins (also indexed by Settings search). page.get() is invoked lazily when the user opens the page. addSearchProvider(Function<String, List<SearchResult>> provider) Background thread Supplies custom entries in Search anything (Shift Shift) for the user's query string. Keep it fast; return an empty list if nothing matches. onActivity(Consumer<Activity.Entry> listener) Swing EDT Notified whenever records are created/changed/deleted, files (PDF/ODT/e-invoice) are exported, or messages/warnings occur. Check entry.draft before finalizing on FILE events. addRecordModifier(DatabaseObjectModifier modifier) Caller thread (typically EDT) Intercepts DatabaseObject lifecycle events (modifyOnSave, modifyOnDelete, executeAfterCreate, executeAfterSave, modifyOnExplode, modifyOnResolve). Throw ChangeNotApprovedException to veto a save or delete. onView(Consumer<DataPanel> listener) Swing EDT Called whenever a record view (DataPanel) opens or displays another record — and immediately for all views already open when the plugin starts. Decorate with badges, banners, or content locks. addJournalExport(JournalExport export) export: EDTadviserPackageEntries: Background Adds an entry to the Journal's Export menu and can contribute extra files (e.g. CSVs) to the tax-adviser ZIP package (JournalAdviserPackage). addTemplateFields(Function<DatabaseObject, Map<String, Object>> provider) Export thread Supplies extra placeholder key -> value pairs when formatting a DatabaseObject for .odt/.fodt/PDF export. Keys map to [key] placeholders in templates. addMailWarningProvider(Function<DatabaseObject, String> provider) Interactive: EDTBatch: Background Called before e-mailing a document. Return a non-empty warning message to ask for confirmation in interactive mode — or log and skip sending in batch mode. Return null/empty for no warning. addEInvoiceSkipRule(Predicate<Item> rule) Export / Mail thread Return true to force plain PDF instead of ZUGFeRD / XRechnung for matching invoices (e.g. VAT-exempt services not subject to e-invoicing mandates). addPrivacyContributor(PrivacyContributor contributor) Caller / Background Integrates plugin-owned personal data with OpenYaBS's GDPR subsystem: additional retention deadlines, Art. 15/20 export ZIP entries, and cleanup on final contact deletion. addLockedDocumentProvider(LockedDocumentProvider provider) Caller / EDT Tells OpenYaBS that a record is locked with an archived original file. Print, PDF, preview, ODT, and e-invoice open the archived file instead of regenerating it, and coordinate stamped duplicates if the archive file is missing. addTranslations(String languageCode, Map<String, String> messages) Any Registers localized key/pattern pairs for this plugin (plugin-ID scoped). languageCode accepts tags like "en", "de", "de_DE", "de-AT". addTranslations(String languageCode, Properties messages) Any Convenience overload accepting java.util.Properties. addTranslationBundle(String languageCode, String resourcePath, ClassLoader loader) Any Loads a UTF-8 .properties file from the plugin JAR classpath (e.g. "/com/example/i18n/messages_de.properties") and registers it for languageCode. onStop(Runnable action) Swing EDT Runs cleanup code when the plugin stops, is disabled, reloaded, or fails mid-start. Can be called multiple times. Works identically in Java and Groovy.

docs.title: ExtensionContext Actions, Helpers, and i18n
docs.text: Method Returns What It Does openTab(String title, JComponent content) void Opens (or focuses) a custom tab in the main OpenYaBS window (automatically marshaled to the Swing EDT). notify(String message) void Displays a short status bar message and logs it in the activity list. notify(String message, DatabaseObject about) void Shows a notification pop-up linked to a specific record (clicking opens the record). popup(String message) void Shows a notification pop-up (and logs it in the activity list). error(String message) void Shows an error/warning notification pop-up. select(String sql) Object[][] Runs a plain SQL SELECT on the YaBS database. Returns Object[][] (never null; empty array on no rows or error — errors are swallowed). execute(String sql) void Runs a plain SQL statement (CREATE TABLE, INSERT, UPDATE, …). Note: For user input, transactions, or strict error handling, use JDBC PreparedStatement (see Example 13). ui(Runnable r) void Executes r immediately if already on the Swing EDT, otherwise via SwingUtilities.invokeLater(r). <T> void background(Supplier<T> work, Consumer<T> then) void Runs work on a daemon thread (plugin-<id>) and passes the result to then on the Swing EDT (then may be null). Uncaught exceptions are logged and displayed via the host error handler. currentView() DataPanel Returns the DataPanel in the currently selected main-window tab, or null. refreshView(DatabaseObject record) void Re-populates record in every open main-window tab currently displaying that record (e.g. after locking or modifying metadata). openFile(File file) void Opens a file with its configured program (for PDFs, respects Settings › External programs). settings() PluginSettings Local key/value store saved on this machine in plugins/<safeId>.properties. dataFolder() File Private folder plugins/<safeId>/ for plugin files (automatically created via mkdirs()). yabsVersion() String Current OpenYaBS version string (e.g. "2.0.17" or "2.0-dev"). language() String Active OpenYaBS UI language tag normalized to ll or ll_CC (e.g. "de", "de_DE", "en"). tr(String key, Object... args) String Resolves a plugin-scoped translation key for the active user language and formats optional MessageFormat placeholders ({0}, {1}, …). Returns key if not found. trOrDefault(String key, String fallback, Object... args) String Same as tr, but uses fallback if key is not registered.

docs.title: Activity.Entry & Activity.Kind (source)
docs.text:
• Activity.Kind: MESSAGE, WARNING, FILE, CREATED, CHANGED, DELETED
  • Fields on Activity.Entry:
  • Date time — timestamp
  • Kind kind — event type
  • String text — display text / filename
  • String detail — localized record type or file owner label (do not match on this for logic; use context instead!)
  • File file — exported file for Kind.FILE, or null
  • Context context — record context (e.g. Context.getInvoice(), Context.getContact()), or null
  • int id — database ID (ids) of the record, or 0
  • boolean draft — true for previews or intermediate PDFs (e.g. before ZUGFeRD embedding); always skip entry.draft when finalizing or archiving!
  • Helper methods: hasRecord(), hasFile(), matches(String needle)

docs.title: DataPanel (source)
docs.text:
Methods relevant to plugins inside onView: - DatabaseObject getDataOwner() — the currently displayed record (Item, Contact, Product, Expense, Revenue, …; check owner != null && owner.__getIDS() > 0 for saved records) - void setDataOwner(DatabaseObject object, boolean populateData) — reloads/shows a record - void setPluginBadge(JComponent badge) — small status badge in the view header next to the record status - void setPluginBanner(JComponent banner) — full-width banner below the toolbar (e.g. status summary + action buttons) - void setContentLocked(boolean locked) / boolean isContentLocked() — disables content fields, line items, and deletion while keeping payment status, reminders, and export usable - void setLockedDocument(File file) / File getLockedDocument() — marks a locked record's archived document on the view (addLockedDocumentProvider is preferred because it works even before a view is refreshed) - boolean hasUnsavedChanges() — whether the user has unsaved edits in the view

OpenYaBS automatically clears pluginBadge, pluginBanner, and contentLocked whenever a view is re-populated or a plugin with an onView listener stops, then re-runs all remaining active onView listeners.

docs.title: DatabaseObjectModifier (source)
docs.text:
• DatabaseObject modifyOnExplode(DatabaseObject object) — called when a record is constructed/loaded
  • DatabaseObject modifyOnSave(DatabaseObject object) throws ChangeNotApprovedException — called before saving; modify fields or throw new ChangeNotApprovedException(object) to cancel the save
  • DatabaseObject executeAfterCreate(DatabaseObject object) — called after a new record is inserted
  • DatabaseObject executeAfterSave(DatabaseObject object) — called after any save
  • Map<String, Object> modifyOnResolve(Map<String, Object> map) — called during reference resolution
  • DatabaseObject modifyOnDelete(DatabaseObject object) throws ChangeNotApprovedException — called before deletion; throw new ChangeNotApprovedException(object) to block deletion

docs.title: JournalExport & JournalExportContext (JournalExport, JournalExportContext)
docs.text:
• JournalExport:
  • String title() — menu item label in the Journal Export menu
  • default String tooltip() — optional tooltip (null by default)
  • void export(JournalExportContext context) — runs on the Swing EDT when selected
  • default Map<String, byte[]> adviserPackageEntries(JournalExportContext context) throws Exception — runs on a background thread during tax-adviser ZIP generation; returns zipPath -> fileBytes (e.g. "myexport/report.csv" -> bytes)
  • JournalExportContext fields:
  • List<JournalCalc.Entry> entries — loaded journal rows (obj, itemId, type, status, net, tax, gross, discount, open, date, number, contact, prename, street, city, country, group, account, description, rates, effect, counted, overpayment)
  • JournalCalc.Totals totals — aggregated totals
  • Date from, Date to — selected reporting period
  • List<String> filters — active filter descriptions
  • Map<BigDecimal, String> rateLabels — VAT rate labels
  • Component parent — parent Swing component for dialogs (may be null in headless/background runs!)
  • Consumer<File> onExported / notifyExported(File file) — call context.notifyExported(file) so the Journal displays a clickable link to the exported file

• default Date retentionUntil(Contact contact) — returns an additional statutory retention end date (e.g. 10 years for medical records), or null
  • default Map<String, String> exportData(Contact contact) — returns extra zipEntryName -> UTF-8 content files (e.g. "myplugin_data.json" -> json) included in the Art. 15/20 GDPR export ZIP

docs.text:
• File lockedDocument(DatabaseObject record) — return the archived original File (even if currently missing on disk) if locked, or null if not locked by this provider
  • default String duplicateRefused(DatabaseObject record) — if the archived file is missing, return a reason string to refuse creating a stamped duplicate, or null to allow
  • default List<String> duplicateWarnings(DatabaseObject record) — return differences between current DB data and the locked snapshot that the user must confirm before creating a duplicate
  • default void duplicateCreated(DatabaseObject record, File missing, File duplicate) — called after a stamped duplicate PDF was created (e.g. to record an audit log entry)

docs.title: 1. Commands, Background Work, and Custom Tabs
docs.text:
Never block the Swing EDT with database queries, file I/O, or HTTP calls. Use ctx.background(work, then) to run slow work off-thread and update the UI safely afterward.

Java:

yabs.addCommand("Revenue Summary", "Opens a summary tab of this year's paid invoices", () -> {
    yabs.background(() -> {
        Object[][] rows = yabs.select(
                "SELECT cnumber, cname, netvalue, taxvalue FROM items "
                + "WHERE inttype = 0 AND intstatus = " + mpv5.db.objects.Item.STATUS_PAID
                + " ORDER BY dateadded DESC");
        return rows;
    }, rows -> {
        String[] cols = {"Number", "Title", "Net", "Tax"};
        javax.swing.JTable table = new javax.swing.JTable(rows, cols);
        table.setAutoCreateRowSorter(true);
        yabs.openTab("Paid Invoices (" + rows.length + ")", new javax.swing.JScrollPane(table));
    });
});

Groovy:

yabs.addCommand('Revenue Summary', 'Opens a summary tab of paid invoices', {
    yabs.background({
        yabs.select("SELECT cnumber, cname, netvalue, taxvalue FROM items WHERE inttype = 0 AND intstatus = ${mpv5.db.objects.Item.STATUS_PAID} ORDER BY dateadded DESC")
    }, { rows ->
        def table = new javax.swing.JTable(rows, ['Number', 'Title', 'Net', 'Tax'] as Object[])
        table.autoCreateRowSorter = true
        yabs.openTab("Paid Invoices (${rows.length})", new javax.swing.JScrollPane(table))
    })
})

docs.title: 2. Settings Pages: Per-Machine vs. Per-Database Config
docs.text:
OpenYaBS gives plugins two configuration mechanisms — pick the right one for your data:

Storage API Scope Best For Local plugin settings ctx.settings().get/set Saved in plugins/<safeId>.properties on this machine only Local paths (archive folder), local ports, window prefs Database global settings mpv5.globals.GlobalSettings.getProperty/setProperty + GlobalSettings.save() Stored in the OpenYaBS database (shared across all users/PCs) Business rules, hourly rates, tax flags, account mappings

Tip: Always prefix GlobalSettings keys with a unique namespace for your plugin (e.g. "myplugin.defaultRate").

Java (settings page using ctx.settings()):

yabs.addSettingsPage("My Plugin", "Configure webhook URL and auto-sync", () -> {
    javax.swing.JPanel panel = new javax.swing.JPanel(new java.awt.GridBagLayout());
    panel.setBorder(javax.swing.BorderFactory.createEmptyBorder(12, 12, 12, 12));
    java.awt.GridBagConstraints g = new java.awt.GridBagConstraints();
    g.insets = new java.awt.Insets(4, 6, 4, 6);
    g.anchor = java.awt.GridBagConstraints.WEST;

    javax.swing.JTextField urlField = new javax.swing.JTextField(yabs.settings().get("webhook.url", ""), 30);
    javax.swing.JCheckBox enabledBox = new javax.swing.JCheckBox("Enable notifications",
            yabs.settings().getBoolean("webhook.enabled", false));
    javax.swing.JButton saveBtn = new javax.swing.JButton("Save");
    saveBtn.addActionListener(e -> {
        yabs.settings().set("webhook.url", urlField.getText().trim());
        yabs.settings().setBoolean("webhook.enabled", enabledBox.isSelected());
        yabs.notify("My Plugin settings saved.");
    });

    g.gridx = 0; g.gridy = 0; panel.add(new javax.swing.JLabel("Webhook URL:"), g);
    g.gridx = 1; panel.add(urlField, g);
    g.gridx = 1; g.gridy = 1; panel.add(enabledBox, g);
    g.gridx = 1; g.gridy = 2; panel.add(saveBtn, g);
    return panel;
});

docs.title: 3. Search Anything Provider
docs.text:
Search providers run on a background thread on every keystroke in Search anything (Shift Shift). Return quickly, require a minimum query length (e.g. >= 2 chars), and cap result counts.

yabs.addSearchProvider(query -> {
    if (query == null || query.trim().length() < 2) {
        return java.util.Collections.emptyList();
    }
    String needle = query.trim().toLowerCase(java.util.Locale.ROOT);
    java.util.List<mpv5.plugin.api.SearchResult> out = new java.util.ArrayList<>();
    for (Vehicle v : loadMatchingVehicles(needle, 10)) {
        out.add(new mpv5.plugin.api.SearchResult(
                v.licensePlate + " — " + v.makeModel,
                "Customer #" + v.contactId + " · Click to open",
                () -> openVehicleDialog(v)));
    }
    return out;
});

docs.title: 4. Reacting to Records and Exported Files (onActivity)
docs.text:
Always check entry.context (locale-independent) rather than entry.detail (localized text), and always check !entry.draft before treating an exported PDF/ODT/XML as a finalized document!

yabs.onActivity(entry -> {
    // 1. React to newly created invoices
    if (entry.kind == mpv5.handler.Activity.Kind.CREATED
            && mpv5.db.common.Context.getInvoice().equals(entry.context)) {
        yabs.notify("Created invoice #" + entry.id + ": " + entry.text);
    }

    // 2. React to issued (non-draft) exported files
    if (entry.kind == mpv5.handler.Activity.Kind.FILE
            && !entry.draft
            && entry.hasFile()
            && mpv5.db.common.Context.getInvoice().equals(entry.context)) {
        // entry.file is the exported PDF, ODT, or ZUGFeRD/XRechnung file
        // Offload heavy I/O or network upload to background():
        java.io.File exported = entry.file;
        int invoiceId = entry.id;
        yabs.background(() -> archiveCopy(invoiceId, exported),
                ok -> yabs.notify("Archived " + exported.getName()));
    }
});

docs.title: 5. Validating and Vetoing Saves or Deletes (addRecordModifier)
docs.text:
Throw new ChangeNotApprovedException(object) from modifyOnSave or modifyOnDelete to cancel the operation cleanly.

Java:

import java.util.Map;
import javax.swing.JOptionPane;
import mpv5.db.common.DatabaseObject;
import mpv5.db.common.DatabaseObjectModifier;
import mpv5.db.objects.Item;
import mpv5.globals.Constants;
import mpv5.ui.panels.ChangeNotApprovedException;

yabs.addRecordModifier(new DatabaseObjectModifier() {
    @Override
    public DatabaseObject modifyOnSave(DatabaseObject object) throws ChangeNotApprovedException {
        if (object instanceof Item) {
            Item item = (Item) object;
            if (item.__getInttype() == Constants.TYPE_INVOICE
                    && (item.__getDescription() == null || item.__getDescription().trim().isEmpty())) {
                int choice = JOptionPane.showConfirmDialog(
                        null,
                        "This invoice has no description. Save anyway?",
                        "Invoice Check",
                        JOptionPane.YES_NO_OPTION,
                        JOptionPane.WARNING_MESSAGE);
                if (choice != JOptionPane.YES_OPTION) {
                    throw new ChangeNotApprovedException(item);
                }
            }
        }
        return object;
    }

    @Override
    public DatabaseObject modifyOnDelete(DatabaseObject object) throws ChangeNotApprovedException {
        // Return object to allow, or throw new ChangeNotApprovedException(object) to block
        return object;
    }

    @Override public DatabaseObject modifyOnExplode(DatabaseObject object) { return object; }
    @Override public DatabaseObject executeAfterCreate(DatabaseObject object) { return object; }
    @Override public DatabaseObject executeAfterSave(DatabaseObject object) { return object; }
    @Override public Map<String, Object> modifyOnResolve(Map<String, Object> map) { return map; }
});

Groovy (map coercion):

import mpv5.db.common.DatabaseObjectModifier
import mpv5.db.objects.Contact
import mpv5.ui.panels.ChangeNotApprovedException

yabs.addRecordModifier([
    modifyOnSave: { obj ->
        if (obj instanceof Contact && obj.__getCname()?.trim()?.isEmpty()) {
            yabs.error('Contact name must not be empty.')
            throw new ChangeNotApprovedException(obj)
        }
        obj
    },
    modifyOnDelete    : { o -> o },
    modifyOnExplode   : { o -> o },
    executeAfterCreate: { o -> o },
    executeAfterSave  : { o -> o },
    modifyOnResolve   : { m -> m }
] as DatabaseObjectModifier)

docs.title: 6. Decorating and Locking Record Views (onView)
docs.text:
Add a header badge, an interactive banner with buttons, or lock content fields on any DataPanel (Invoices, Contacts, Products, Expenses, Revenues…).

import java.awt.Color;
import java.awt.FlowLayout;
import javax.swing.BorderFactory;
import javax.swing.JButton;
import javax.swing.JLabel;
import javax.swing.JPanel;
import mpv5.db.common.DatabaseObject;
import mpv5.db.objects.Item;

yabs.onView(view -> {
    DatabaseObject owner = view.getDataOwner();
    if (!(owner instanceof Item) || owner.__getIDS() <= 0) {
        return;
    }
    Item invoice = (Item) owner;

    // 1. Header badge next to status
    if (invoice.__getIntstatus() == Item.STATUS_PAID) {
        JLabel badge = new JLabel("  PAID  ");
        badge.setOpaque(true);
        badge.setBackground(new Color(220, 252, 231));
        badge.setForeground(new Color(22, 101, 52));
        view.setPluginBadge(badge);
    }

    // 2. Banner with action button below toolbar
    JPanel banner = new JPanel(new FlowLayout(FlowLayout.LEFT, 8, 4));
    banner.setBackground(new Color(239, 246, 255));
    banner.setBorder(BorderFactory.createMatteBorder(0, 0, 1, 0, new Color(147, 197, 253)));
    banner.add(new JLabel("Custom metadata for " + invoice.__getCnumber()));
    JButton editBtn = new JButton("Edit details…");
    editBtn.addActionListener(e -> {
        // After modifying plugin data, refresh all open views of this record:
        yabs.refreshView(invoice);
    });
    banner.add(editBtn);
    view.setPluginBanner(banner);

    // 3. Optionally lock content fields & deletion (payment status & export remain enabled)
    // view.setContentLocked(true);
});

docs.title: 7. Custom Template Placeholders (addTemplateFields)
docs.text:
Expose custom fields from your plugin to any LibreOffice .odt or .fodt template!

  • Every entry "myplugin.fieldName" -> value in the returned map becomes usable as [myplugin.fieldName] in templates.
  • Always namespace keys with a short plugin prefix (myplugin.*) so they never collide with built-in fields (item.*, contact.*, companyinfo.*, template.*).
  • Return "" (empty string) rather than null for missing optional fields so placeholders don't remain literal [myplugin.foo] text in exported PDFs.
yabs.addTemplateFields(obj -> {
    java.util.Map<String, Object> fields = new java.util.LinkedHashMap<>();
    if (obj instanceof mpv5.db.objects.Item) {
        mpv5.db.objects.Item item = (mpv5.db.objects.Item) obj;
        fields.put("myplugin.projectCode", loadProjectCode(item.__getIDS())); // "" if none
        fields.put("myplugin.contactRef", "C-" + item.__getContactsids());
    }
    return fields;
});

Bundling & exporting starter .fodt templates (Java): Place .fodt files under src/main/resources/com/example/myplugin/templates/ and offer a command that saves them via MyPlugin.class.getResourceAsStream(...) and mpv5.ui.dialogs.DialogForFile (see WorkshopPlugin.java for a full example).

docs.title: 8. Journal Export and Tax-Adviser ZIP (addJournalExport)
docs.text:
Contribute both an interactive export format in the Journal's Export menu and automatic files inside the tax-adviser ZIP package:

import java.io.File;
import java.nio.charset.StandardCharsets;
import java.nio.file.Files;
import java.util.Collections;
import java.util.Map;
import mpv5.handler.JournalCalc;
import mpv5.plugin.api.JournalExport;
import mpv5.plugin.api.JournalExportContext;
import mpv5.ui.dialogs.DialogForFile;

yabs.addJournalExport(new JournalExport() {
    @Override
    public String title() {
        return "Custom Accounting CSV";
    }

    @Override
    public String tooltip() {
        return "Exports counted journal entries as semicolon-separated UTF-8 CSV.";
    }

    @Override
    public void export(JournalExportContext ctx) {
        DialogForFile chooser = new DialogForFile(DialogForFile.FILES_ONLY, "custom-journal.csv");
        if (!chooser.saveFile()) {
            return;
        }
        try {
            File target = chooser.getFile();
            Files.write(target.toPath(), renderCsv(ctx).getBytes(StandardCharsets.UTF_8));
            ctx.notifyExported(target); // shows clickable file link in Journal
            yabs.notify("Exported " + target.getName());
        } catch (Exception e) {
            yabs.error("Export failed: " + e.getMessage());
        }
    }

    @Override
    public Map<String, byte[]> adviserPackageEntries(JournalExportContext ctx) {
        byte[] bytes = renderCsv(ctx).getBytes(StandardCharsets.UTF_8);
        return Collections.singletonMap("custom/journal.csv", bytes);
    }

    private String renderCsv(JournalExportContext ctx) {
        StringBuilder sb = new StringBuilder("Date;Number;Contact;Net;Tax;Gross\n");
        for (JournalCalc.Entry e : ctx.entries) {
            if (!e.counted) {
                continue;
            }
            sb.append(e.date).append(';')
              .append(e.number).append(';')
              .append(e.contact).append(';')
              .append(e.net).append(';')
              .append(e.tax).append(';')
              .append(e.gross).append('\n');
        }
        return sb.toString();
    }
});

docs.title: 9. Pre-Send E-Mail Warnings and E-Invoice Skip Rules
docs.text:
Useful for privacy-sensitive documents (e.g. medical diagnoses under Art. 9 GDPR) or VAT-exempt invoices where e-invoicing does not apply:

// 1. Warn before e-mailing a document (interactive: YES/NO dialog; batch: logged & skipped)
yabs.addMailWarningProvider(obj -> {
    if (obj instanceof mpv5.db.objects.Item) {
        mpv5.db.objects.Item item = (mpv5.db.objects.Item) obj;
        if (containsConfidentialNotes(item.__getIDS())) {
            return "This invoice contains confidential notes. Send via unencrypted e-mail anyway?";
        }
    }
    return null; // no warning
});

// 2. Skip ZUGFeRD / XRechnung generation and fall back to plain PDF
yabs.addEInvoiceSkipRule(item -> isExemptFromEInvoice(item.__getIDS()));

docs.title: 10. GDPR Retention, Export, and Final Deletion (addPrivacyContributor)
docs.text:
If your plugin stores personal data linked to a Contact, register a PrivacyContributor so OpenYaBS's GDPR tools (Data protection / GDPR) automatically enforce your retention period, include your data in Art. 15/20 exports, and erase your rows on final deletion:

import java.util.Collections;
import java.util.Date;
import java.util.Map;
import mpv5.db.objects.Contact;
import mpv5.plugin.api.PrivacyContributor;

yabs.addPrivacyContributor(new PrivacyContributor() {
    @Override
    public Date retentionUntil(Contact contact) {
        // Return a Date if your plugin requires keeping this contact longer, else null
        return loadRetentionEndDate(contact.__getIDS());
    }

    @Override
    public Map<String, String> exportData(Contact contact) {
        String json = exportPluginRecordsAsJson(contact.__getIDS());
        if (json == null) {
            return Collections.emptyMap();
        }
        return Collections.singletonMap("myplugin_contact_data.json", json);
    }

    @Override
    public void onDeleteFinally(Contact contact) {
        deletePluginRecordsForContact(contact.__getIDS());
    }
});

docs.title: 11. Archived Originals for Locked Records (addLockedDocumentProvider)
docs.text:
When a plugin finalizes/locks a record with an archived PDF or e-invoice, register a LockedDocumentProvider. Whenever the user clicks Print, PDF, Preview, ODT, or E-invoice, OpenYaBS asks all providers and opens the archived original instead of regenerating the file — even if the view was not refreshed yet. If the archived file is missing on disk, OpenYaBS offers a stamped duplicate controlled by the provider:

import java.io.File;
import java.util.List;
import mpv5.db.common.DatabaseObject;
import mpv5.plugin.api.LockedDocumentProvider;

yabs.addLockedDocumentProvider(new LockedDocumentProvider() {
    @Override
    public File lockedDocument(DatabaseObject record) {
        return findArchivedFileOrNull(record); // return File even if !file.exists()
    }

    @Override
    public String duplicateRefused(DatabaseObject record) {
        return hasTamperedData(record) ? "Record data no longer matches locked hash." : null;
    }

    @Override
    public List<String> duplicateWarnings(DatabaseObject record) {
        return findCustomerAddressDifferences(record); // user must confirm before duplicate
    }

    @Override
    public void duplicateCreated(DatabaseObject record, File missing, File duplicate) {
        logDuplicateAuditEntry(record, missing, duplicate);
    }
});

docs.title: 12. Multi-Language Plugins and i18n (addTranslationBundle, tr)
docs.text:
OpenYaBS provides a built-in, plugin-ID-scoped translation system with java.text.MessageFormat support ({0}, {1}, …) and automatic cleanup on stop.

Fallback chain: exact locale (de_AT) → base language (de, automatically normalizing OpenYaBS names like DE-Yabs-2.0) → en → fallback (for trOrDefault) → key.

Java (UTF-8 .properties bundles in JAR resources):

src/main/resources/com/example/myplugin/i18n/messages_en.properties: 

plugin.name=My Plugin
cmd.hello.title=Say hello
cmd.hello.msg=Hello {0}, running on OpenYaBS {1}!

src/main/resources/com/example/myplugin/i18n/messages_de.properties: 

plugin.name=Mein Plugin
cmd.hello.title=Hallo sagen
cmd.hello.msg=Hallo {0}, OpenYaBS {1} läuft!

Register in start(ExtensionContext yabs): 

ClassLoader cl = MyPlugin.class.getClassLoader();
yabs.addTranslationBundle("en", "/com/example/myplugin/i18n/messages_en.properties", cl);
yabs.addTranslationBundle("de", "/com/example/myplugin/i18n/messages_de.properties", cl);

String msg = yabs.tr("cmd.hello.msg", "Alice", yabs.yabsVersion());
String activeLang = yabs.language(); // e.g. "de", "de_DE", "en"

Groovy (inline maps): 

yabs.addTranslations('en', [greet: 'Hello {0}!', title: 'My Tool'])
yabs.addTranslations('de', [greet: 'Hallo {0}!', title: 'Mein Werkzeug'])

yabs.addCommand(yabs.tr('title'), '', {
    yabs.notify(yabs.tr('greet', 'World'))
})

docs.title: 13. Custom Database Tables and Cross-Database JDBC
docs.text:
OpenYaBS supports H2 (default, in Derby compatibility mode), Apache Derby, MySQL / MariaDB, and PostgreSQL.

  • ctx.select(sql) and ctx.execute(sql) are convenient for quick queries, but they take plain SQL strings and swallow SQL errors.
  • For production plugins that create their own tables or accept user input, use JDBC PreparedStatement on OpenYaBS's database connection and always guard with hasDatabase() (so your plugin doesn't fail during headless tests or before DB login):
import java.sql.Connection;
import java.sql.PreparedStatement;
import java.sql.ResultSet;
import java.sql.SQLException;
import java.sql.Statement;
import mpv5.db.common.DatabaseConnection;

public static boolean hasDatabase() {
    try {
        return DatabaseConnection.getConnector() != null
                && DatabaseConnection.getConnector().getConnection() != null;
    } catch (Throwable t) {
        return false;
    }
}

public static Connection connection() throws SQLException {
    DatabaseConnection dc = DatabaseConnection.getConnector();
    Connection c = dc == null ? null : dc.getConnection();
    if (c == null) {
        throw new SQLException("No active OpenYaBS database connection");
    }
    return c;
}

public static void initSchema(Connection conn) throws SQLException {
    // Prefix table names with your plugin short name!
    // Use portable SQL types: INT, BIGINT, VARCHAR(...), CLOB/TEXT, TIMESTAMP.
    try (Statement st = conn.createStatement()) {
        st.execute("CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS myp_notes ("
                + "item_id INT PRIMARY KEY, "
                + "note VARCHAR(2000) NOT NULL, "
                + "updated_at VARCHAR(32) NOT NULL)");
    } catch (SQLException e) {
        // Apache Derby < 10.15 lacks IF NOT EXISTS (SQLState X0Y32 = table already exists)
        if (!"X0Y32".equalsIgnoreCase(e.getSQLState())) {
            throw e;
        }
    }
}

Cross-database SQL tips: - Prefix all custom tables with a unique plugin prefix (e.g. ws_, hp_, verein_, gobd_). - Never concatenate user input into SQL — always use ? placeholders in PreparedStatement. - Do not close OpenYaBS's shared Connection! Only close your Statement, PreparedStatement, and ResultSet (via try-with-resources). - Avoid DB-specific UPSERT syntax (ON CONFLICT, MERGE, ON DUPLICATE KEY); a portable pattern is UPDATE ... WHERE id = ? and if executeUpdate() == 0, run INSERT INTO .... - Store ISO dates as VARCHAR(10) (YYYY-MM-DD) if you want identical behavior across H2, Derby, MySQL, and PostgreSQL without timezone surprises.

docs.title: 14. Working with OpenYaBS Domain Objects (DatabaseObject, Context)
docs.text:
Common OpenYaBS classes you will frequently use in plugins:

Task Code Fetch one record by ID Item inv = (Item) DatabaseObject.getObject(Context.getInvoice(), itemId); Fetch all records of a type ArrayList<DatabaseObject> list = DatabaseObject.getObjects(Context.getContact()); Create & save a new record Product p = new Product(); p.setInttype(Product.TYPE_SERVICE); p.setCnumber("SVC-1"); p.setCname("Consulting"); p.setExternalnetvalue(new BigDecimal("100.00")); p.save(true); Read invoice line items SubItem[] lines = item.getSubitems(); Read invoice totals item.getGrossAmount(), item.getNetAfterDiscount(), item.__getNetvalue(), item.__getTaxvalue() Current logged-in user User u = User.getCurrentUser(); Open a record in a tab mpv5.YabsViewProxy.instance().getIdentifierView().addTab(record);

Common Context factories (mpv5.db.common.Context): getInvoice(), getOrder(), getOffer(), getDelivery(), getConfirmation(), getCredit(), getPartPayment(), getDeposit(), getContact(), getCustomer(), getSupplier(), getProduct(), getProductGroup(), getSubItem(), getExpense(), getRevenue(), getTaxes(), getAccounts(), getGroup(), getUser(), getTemplate(), getSchedule(), getConversation().

Common document type constants (mpv5.globals.Constants): TYPE_INVOICE (0), TYPE_ORDER (1), TYPE_OFFER (2), TYPE_DELIVERY_NOTE (3), TYPE_ORDER_CONFIRMATION (4), TYPE_CREDIT (20), TYPE_PART_PAYMENT (21), TYPE_DEPOSIT (22), TYPE_EXPENSE (18), TYPE_REVENUE (19), TYPE_PAYMENT (23), TYPE_CANCELLATION (24).

Common Item status constants (mpv5.db.objects.Item): STATUS_QUEUED, STATUS_IN_PROGRESS, STATUS_PAUSED, STATUS_FINISHED, STATUS_PAID, STATUS_CANCELLED.

docs.title: Threading, Bundled Libraries, and Best Practices
Threading Summary
docs.text: Callback / Method Thread Rule YabsExtension.start, stop, onStop Swing EDT Keep fast; offload heavy startup queries to ctx.background(...). addCommand action Swing EDT Keep fast; use ctx.background(...) for DB/file/network work. addSettingsPage supplier Swing EDT Safe to create Swing components directly. onActivity, onView Swing EDT Safe to update DataPanel badges/banners; avoid slow queries. addSearchProvider Background thread Must be thread-safe and fast; do not touch Swing components directly (its SearchResult.open runs on EDT when selected). JournalExport.export Swing EDT Safe to open dialogs; use background(...) for heavy exports. JournalExport.adviserPackageEntries Background thread Must NOT show modal Swing dialogs (ctx.parent may be null). background(work, then) work: Daemon threadthen: Swing EDT Standard way to perform slow work and display results.

docs.title: Libraries Already Bundled in OpenYaBS (lib/ & Runtime)
docs.text:
Plugins automatically inherit OpenYaBS's classpath (parent classloader). Notable libraries already available at runtime (use compileOnly in Java, or import directly in Groovy):

  • Java 21 standard library (java.net.http.HttpClient, java.time.*, javax.crypto.*, etc.)
  • Apache Groovy 4.0.24 (excluding Apache Ivy / @Grab)
  • Jackson 2.22 (com.fasterxml.jackson.databind.ObjectMapper — JSON reading/writing)
  • Apache PDFBox 3.0.8 (PDF inspection, creation, stamping)
  • Apache Commons IO 2.17, Commons Lang, Commons Codec
  • FlatLaf 3.5.4 (modern Swing Look & Feel)
  • ODFDOM / XDocReport (ODT document handling)
  • Mustangproject (ZUGFeRD / XRechnung e-invoice libraries)
  • H2 2.3, Derby, PostgreSQL, MySQL JDBC drivers

docs.title: UI Styling Helpers
docs.text: To make your settings pages and tabs match OpenYaBS's look and feel (including Dark Mode and HiDPI scaling), you can optionally reuse OpenYaBS's Swing helpers: - mpv5.ui.modern.ModernTheme (px(int) for HiDPI scaling, font(delta, style), accent(), muted(), roomy(JTextField)) - mpv5.ui.modern.Card, mpv5.ui.modern.Applets, mpv5.ui.modern.PrimaryButton (see CashRegister.java) - mpv5.ui.dialogs.DialogForFile (file/directory save & open dialogs)

docs.title: Headless JUnit 5 Unit Tests (No GUI Needed!)
docs.text:
ExtensionManager can be instantiated directly in unit tests with a temporary folder and a minimal stub Host — making it fast and reliable to test registration, commands, search providers, i18n, template fields, stop cleanup, and JAR packaging:

import static org.junit.jupiter.api.Assertions.*;

import java.nio.file.Path;
import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.List;
import javax.swing.JComponent;
import mpv5.plugin.ExtensionManager;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.io.TempDir;

class HelloPluginTest {

    @TempDir
    Path tempDir;

    static final class StubHost implements ExtensionManager.Host {
        final List<String> messages = new ArrayList<>();
        final List<String> errors = new ArrayList<>();
        @Override public void openTab(String title, JComponent content) {}
        @Override public void notify(String message) { messages.add(message); }
        @Override public void ui(Runnable r) { r.run(); }
        @Override public void changed() {}
        @Override public void error(String plugin, Throwable t) { errors.add(plugin + ": " + t); }
    }

    @Test
    void startsRegistersCommandTranslatesAndCleansUpOnStop() {
        StubHost host = new StubHost();
        ExtensionManager mgr = new ExtensionManager(tempDir.toFile(), host);

        ExtensionManager.Installed inst = mgr.register(new HelloPlugin());
        assertTrue(mgr.start(inst));
        assertEquals(ExtensionManager.State.RUNNING, inst.getState());
        assertEquals(1, mgr.commands().size());
        assertTrue(host.errors.isEmpty());

        // Test localized output across locales
        assertEquals("Hallo sagen", mgr.translateForLocale(HelloPlugin.ID, "de_DE", "cmd.greet.title", null));
        assertEquals("Say hello", mgr.translateForLocale(HelloPlugin.ID, "en", "cmd.greet.title", null));

        // Execute command
        mgr.commands().get(0).action.run();
        assertFalse(host.messages.isEmpty());

        // Stop removes all contributions
        mgr.stop(inst);
        assertEquals(0, mgr.contributions(HelloPlugin.ID));
        assertTrue(mgr.commands().isEmpty());
    }
}

For custom SQL tables, test your Store class directly against an in-memory H2 database:

try (Connection conn = DriverManager.getConnection("jdbc:h2:mem:plugintest;MODE=Derby;DB_CLOSE_DELAY=-1")) {
    MyPluginStore.initSchema(conn);
    // insert, query, update, assert...
}

docs.title: Debugging Tips
docs.text:
• Groovy Console (Settings › GroovyConsole): Great interactive scratchpad to inspect live DatabaseObjects, test Context queries, or try Swing components against your running database.
  • Built-in Plugin Editor (F5): Catches Groovy syntax errors and jumps directly to the line number.
  • Plugin Manager error column: If a plugin enters FAILED, its exception class and message are shown directly in Settings › Plugins.
  • Logging: Call mpv5.logging.Log.Debug(MyPlugin.class, "details or exception") to write to OpenYaBS's log file.

docs.title: Developing Plugins with AI Coding Agents
docs.text: OpenYaBS's plugin system is designed to work smoothly with AI coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Antigravity, GitHub Copilot, etc.): the entire public API is a small set of clean interfaces in mpv5.plugin.api, plugins can be verified headlessly with ExtensionManager and in-memory H2, and five full-featured official Java plugins live right inside the OpenYaBS repository as reference examples.

docs.title: Starter Prompt: Groovy Plugin (Fast Automation)
docs.text:
Copy, customize the Goal section, and paste into your AI agent:

Write a single-file OpenYaBS Groovy plugin (.groovy) following the OpenYaBS Plugin Developer Guide:
https://github.com/anti43/openyabs/wiki/Writing-plugins-(EN)

Goal:
<Describe what your plugin should do, e.g. "Add a command that exports all unpaid invoices older than 30 days to a CSV file, and show a red badge on overdue invoices when opened.">

Requirements:
- Include header metadata comments at the very top: // @id, // @name, // @description, // @version, // @author, // @minYabsVersion 2.0.10.
- Use the bound `yabs` (mpv5.plugin.api.ExtensionContext) variable.
- Do NOT use @Grab (Ivy is not bundled). Only use JDK 21, Groovy 4, and OpenYaBS classes.
- Match record types via mpv5.db.common.Context (e.g. Context.getInvoice()) and mpv5.globals.Constants.TYPE_*, never on localized strings like "Rechnung".
- In onActivity, check !entry.draft before reacting to FILE events.
- Offload slow DB/file/network work to yabs.background({ ... }, { ... }) so the Swing EDT stays responsive.
- Provide clean error handling and register any cleanup in onStop = { ... }.

docs.title: Starter Prompt: Java Plugin (Full Module with Gradle & Tests)
docs.text:
Copy, customize the Goal section, and paste into your AI agent:

Create an OpenYaBS Java plugin project (Gradle, Java 21) following the OpenYaBS Plugin Developer Guide:
https://github.com/anti43/openyabs/wiki/Writing-plugins-(EN)

Reference official plugins in https://github.com/anti43/openyabs/tree/master/plugins (especially plugins/workshop and plugins/verein).

Goal:
<Describe your domain plugin: custom tables, UI banners/dialogs, settings page, commands, template placeholders, exports, validations, etc.>

Technical requirements:
1. Implement mpv5.plugin.api.YabsExtension (target Java 21, minYabsVersion "2.0.10") and register it in src/main/resources/META-INF/services/mpv5.plugin.api.YabsExtension.
2. Separate concerns cleanly: *Plugin (entry point), *Store (cross-DB JDBC with PreparedStatement & GlobalSettings), *Validator (pure testable logic + template fields), *Ui (Swing panels/dialogs).
3. Guard DB initialization with hasDatabase() so start(ctx) succeeds cleanly in headless tests and handles database switches.
4. Use OpenYaBS's plugin i18n API (addTranslationBundle + ctx.tr) with UTF-8 messages_en.properties and messages_de.properties (identical key sets).
5. Prefix custom DB tables and template placeholder keys (e.g. [myplugin.*]) with a unique plugin namespace. Return "" instead of null for empty template fields.
6. Never close OpenYaBS's shared JDBC Connection; only close Statement/PreparedStatement/ResultSet.
7. Write JUnit 5 tests covering: ServiceLoader discovery, translation bundle key parity, pure validator/template logic, SQL store against in-memory H2 (jdbc:h2:mem:...;MODE=Derby), and headless ExtensionManager start/stop lifecycle.
8. Verify with `./gradlew test jar` and confirm META-INF/services/mpv5.plugin.api.YabsExtension is inside the built JAR.

docs.title: AI Agent Pitfalls Checklist
docs.text:
When reviewing or prompting AI-generated plugins, watch out for these common mistakes:

  1. Wrong plugin API package: Use mpv5.plugin.api.YabsExtension + ExtensionContext, never the deprecated mpv5.pluginhandling.YabsPlugin / plugin.Main.
  2. Missing ServiceLoader file: Java JARs must contain META-INF/services/mpv5.plugin.api.YabsExtension (exact filename!) with the fully qualified class name.
  3. Header comments placed after import in Groovy: Groovy @name/@id tags are only parsed at the very top of the file before the first code/import line.
  4. Using @Grab in Groovy: Apache Ivy is excluded from OpenYaBS; @Grab will fail. Use Java + Gradle if you need extra libraries.
  5. Matching localized strings in onActivity: Check Context.getInvoice().equals(entry.context) instead of entry.detail == "Rechnung" (breaks in other UI languages).
  6. Ignoring entry.draft: Previews and intermediate PDFs emit Activity.Kind.FILE with entry.draft == true. Always skip drafts for archiving/finalization.
  7. Blocking the Swing EDT: Put slow DB queries, file exports, or HTTP requests inside ctx.background(work, then).
  8. Not guarding hasDatabase() in start(ctx): Headless tests and pre-login/DB-switch lifecycles may call start(ctx) when no DB connection is active.
  9. Closing the shared JDBC Connection: Never put DatabaseConnection.getConnector().getConnection() in a try (...) block! Closing it breaks OpenYaBS's database session.
  10. Wrong settings scope: ctx.settings() is local to one computer (plugins/<id>.properties); use GlobalSettings for business configuration shared across a multi-user database.
  11. Forgetting ChangeNotApprovedException constructor argument: Use throw new ChangeNotApprovedException(object) (it takes the DatabaseObject, not a String message — show a message via JOptionPane or ctx.error(...) first).
  12. Leaving unreplaced [myplugin.key] placeholders: Always populate every documented template key with "" when empty instead of omitting it or returning null.

docs.text:
When building a plugin (yourself or with an AI agent), study the official open-source plugins in the OpenYaBS repository — each demonstrates clean patterns for different parts of the API:

docs.title: Classic Plugins (Legacy)
docs.text: Plugins from older YaBS versions (a class plugin.Main implementing mpv5.pluginhandling.YabsPlugin, stored inside the database per user) remain supported for backward compatibility and appear at the bottom of Settings › Plugins under Classic plugins (database) (click Show). Do not use the classic API for new plugins — always implement mpv5.plugin.api.YabsExtension (Java) or write a .groovy plugin script.
